title: Product of Array Except Self
statement:
Given an integer array `nums`, return an array `answer` of the same length where `answer[i]` is the product of every element of `nums` **other than** `nums[i]`.

You may **not** use division, and your solution must run in **O(n)** time. The product of any subset of `nums` is guaranteed to fit in a 32-bit `int`.
constraints: every prefix and suffix product fits in an int

target.note: O(1) extra space besides the output array

hints: answer[i] is (everything to the left of i) × (everything to the right of i). Can you know either of those for every i without recomputing it?
Precompute running products: prefix[i] = product of nums[0..i-1] and suffix[i] = product of nums[i+1..n-1]. Then answer[i] = prefix[i] · suffix[i]. That's two linear passes.
Use the output array as the prefix array in a left-to-right pass, then walk right-to-left carrying a single running suffix product and multiply it in. Zeros need no special handling.
followups: Can you do it with O(1) extra space, not counting the output array?
If division were allowed, how would you handle one zero? Two zeros?
What changes if the products might overflow a long — how would you return the answers modulo 10^9 + 7?
explain: Split answer[i] into the product of everything left of i and everything right of i. Pass one, left to right: write the running prefix product into answer[i] before multiplying nums[i] into it. Pass two, right to left: keep a running suffix product, multiply it into answer[i], then multiply nums[i] into the suffix. Every element is touched twice, so it's O(n) time and O(1) extra space beyond the output. It needs no division, so zeros just work: one zero leaves a single non-zero entry and two zeros make everything zero. The brute force multiplies n-1 numbers for each i, which is O(n^2).
